answer: Deposits are visible in saffron, and ember reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 22% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, anyone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 141 aliases, and each one needs its own funded wharf account. Each duplicate costs another 79 dollars in locked collateral and another 8 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
